key_insight: FiLIP trains CT representations using report-derived abnormal findings rather than treating different patients’ scans and reports as negative pairs.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support CT finding recognition and automated report generation, but clinical utility remains to be established.
method: Use a large language model to extract abnormal finding phrases from radiology reports.
Encode findings with a biomedical text embedding model to create explicit training targets.
Train the CT image encoder to learn these findings-aware semantic representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better multi-label zero-shot finding classification than weakly supervised approaches on in-domain and external-domain evaluations, plus effective fine-tuning for report generation.
watch_item: Training depends on report-derived findings; extraction errors or omitted findings could affect learned representations.
paper_title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
